subject.title: tools.exec.approvalRunningNoticeMs is documented but rejected by the 2026.3.24 config schema

question: Should maintainers adopt/rebase the open fork PR, replace it with a narrow upstream repair, or close that candidate before allowing a new fix path?
rationale: Current main remains broken, but the open closing-reference PR is conflicting and not maintainer-editable, so automation should not create a competing branch until maintainers choose how to handle that candidate.

options.title: Replace with narrow upstream repair
options.body: Close or supersede the conflicting fork candidate and land the minimal schema repair in an editable upstream PR.

options.title: Adopt and rebase the fork PR
options.body: Work with the fork PR owner or manually carry the same patch forward while preserving appropriate credit.

options.title: Keep waiting on the fork PR
options.body: Leave the issue open with no new repair work until the fork author makes the branch clean and reviewable.

recommendation.title: Replace with narrow upstream repair
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the conflicting fork candidate and land the minimal schema repair in an editable upstream PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant config/docs behavior and schema refactor history both route through this area, and the needed choice is maintainer-side PR handling rather than a new product decision.
